device: Audiotec-Fischer Helix DSP Ultra S, output layer, 96 kHz
question: does the processor's Butterworth 24 dB/oct match the model in Resonalyze's CrossoverFilter.cs (two RBJ biquads, Q = 1.3066 and 0.5412, high-pass sharing the low-pass denominator)
rig: ELECTRICAL loop, no microphone: Scarlett 2i2 out L -> Helix line in, Helix line out -> Scarlett in 1; out R -> in 2 direct as the timing reference, timing offset 0. A spare output, not one the working tune uses, so the channel is configured from scratch; nothing but the crossover changed within the set, so the ratio to the set's reference is the filter alone.
why_460: the frequency the working preset uses on the mids, not a synthetic round number - so the check lands where the tune actually sits
levels: REW electrical dB; only ratios within a set carry meaning
resampling: REW raw unsmoothed spectrum (linear bins), complex-averaged into each 1/96-octave cell with the measurement's own delay removed before averaging and restored after
provenance: captured and exported by the research session (ayukhno/autosound-research, commit 92e83ab, datasets/rew/bw24-460-2026-09-04); resample() and grid() imported from this project's own export-bench3.py, not reimplemented, so the files land on the same grid as every other set here. Copied in verbatim.

files.what: crossover configured at 460 Hz and BYPASSED - the set's reference
high-pass 460 Hz, Butterworth 24 dB/oct - the filter under test

high-pass 460 Hz, Linkwitz-Riley 24 dB/oct - the control. LR24 is verified separately against the model at 1 kHz (fact 8), so it says whether the rig and the model code are sound before the Butterworth number is read
the reference again at the end of the pass - drift over the four sweeps
